deep.reconstruction:
This page is the first example (Ex 1) in Grothendieck's notes on 'analyseurs'. The previous and next pages are IBM job listings dated 82.109, i.e. 19 April 1982, which fits the archive date '[à partir de 1982]'.

The axioms are on earlier pages not given here, so the definition has to be inferred. An analyseur Ω seems to be a set with three operations:
- a commutative 'pré-anneau' structure (+, ·), where pré-anneau means not necessarily unital;
- an associative composition ∘ with a unit;
- compatibility conditions 1°), 2°) between them, presumably right distributivity (F+G)∘H = F∘H + G∘H and (FG)∘H = (F∘H)(G∘H);
- a further condition 3°), whose content is not visible on this page.
The 'constants' are the elements c with c∘λ = c for all λ. They form a sub-pré-anneau Ω_0.

In modern terms this is essentially a (commutative) composition ring, or tri-operational algebra: the one-variable part of an algebraic theory carrying a commutative ring structure.

Examples on the page:
(1) For a commutative pré-anneau A, Ω_A = App(A,A) (all maps A→A) with pointwise + and ·, and ∘ = composition with unit id_A. Conditions 1°) and 2°) hold. The constants are the constant maps, so Ω_0 ≅ A. Ω_A is unital iff A is.
(2) Variant: for a k-algebra A, take Ω_{A/k} = End(W_k(A)). This is most plausibly the Demazure–Gabriel k-functor W(A): R ↦ A⊗_k R, with End taken as k-functors or schemes, not as groups. Ω_{A/k} is then the ring of polynomial self-maps of A, again with Ω_0 ≅ A. The point is to avoid the degeneracy of set-theoretic maps.
(3) Topos version: for a commutative Anneau 𝒜 in a topos, Ω(𝒜) = End_{sheaves of sets}(𝒜), with xy and x∘y. A circled margin question asks whether (Ω_𝒜)_0 ≅ Γ𝒜.
(4) For A = k, Ω ≅ k[T] with the usual addition, multiplication and substitution. Condition 3°) holds and the constants are k.
(5) A tentative variant is k[[T]]^+, power series without constant term, with product and composition; its constants reduce to 0. Composition is not defined if constant terms are allowed, hence the hesitation in the note.

The page ends with a general construction. For any analyseur Ω, the map F ↦ (λ ↦ F∘λ), Ω → App(Ω_0,Ω_0) = Ω_{Ω_0}, is a homomorphism of analyseurs and is an isomorphism on constants. One is 'content' when it is injective: Ω is then 'functional', i.e. a sub-analyseur of a standard one. The margin seems to name the standard examples 'analyseurs ensemblistes' or 'standard' over a pré-anneau.

The problem served appears to be an axiomatization of 'rings of functions closed under composition' (polynomial, analytic, smooth, etc.). It is compared against the canonical set-theoretic model, with a representation theorem in the style of Cayley.
errors: No outright error, but the hope for injectivity of Ω → App(Ω_0,Ω_0) already fails for Ω = k[T] with k a finite field (T^q − T ↦ 0). This is presumably why the scheme-theoretic variant End(W_k(A)) is introduced.

The circled question (Ω_𝒜)_0 ≅ Γ𝒜 has a positive answer. If F∘λ = F for all λ, take λ = the constant 0, i.e. 𝒜→1→𝒜 (it exists because 𝒜 has the global section 0). Then F = F∘0 factors through the global section F(0); conversely, maps factoring through a global section are constants. So constants = Γ𝒜, provided End means global endomorphisms; with the internal Hom one would instead get 𝒜 itself.
Unclear in the manuscript: for k[[T]]^+ the 'constants' are only 0, so Ω_0 = 0 and the representation into App(Ω_0,Ω_0) is trivial, as the note seems to observe.

The precise content of conditions 1°)–3°) is not on this page, so verifying 'Les conditions 1°) et 2°) sont vérifiées' depends on the earlier definitions. Under the natural reading (right distributivity of ∘ over + and ·) the verification is immediate.

ideas.what: Analyseur: a commutative pré-anneau with an associative unital composition, right-distributive over + and ·, with a sub-pré-anneau of constants
ideas.modern_name: composition ring / tri-operational algebra; the one-variable part of a Lawvere theory over commutative rings
ideas.usually_credited_to: K. Menger (tri-operational algebras, 1950s); I. Adler, 'Composition rings' (Duke Math. J. 1962); near-ring literature (Pilz)

ideas.what: Standard (set-theoretic) analyseur App(A,A) of a commutative pré-anneau, with constants ≅ A
ideas.modern_name: ring of all self-maps with pointwise operations and composition (full function composition ring)

ideas.what: Scheme-theoretic variant End(W_k(A)) for a k-algebra A, avoiding the degeneracy of set maps
ideas.modern_name: polynomial self-maps of the k-functor W(A) (Demazure–Gabriel); polynomial-function composition rings

ideas.what: Topos version: Ω(𝒜) = End of the underlying sheaf of a ring object 𝒜, with constants ≅ Γ𝒜
ideas.modern_name: composition ring of endomorphisms of a ring object in a topos (one-variable internal algebraic theory)

ideas.what: k[T] with substitution as the basic example, and k[[T]]^+ as a non-unital variant
ideas.modern_name: free one-variable composition ring / formal power series composition

ideas.what: Canonical homomorphism Ω → App(Ω_0,Ω_0), F ↦ (λ ↦ F∘λ), an isomorphism on constants; injectivity singles out 'functional' analyseurs
ideas.modern_name: Cayley-type functional representation of a composition ring

missed.claim: Grothendieck's analyseurs, especially the scheme-theoretic variant End(W_k(A)) and the topos variant, are close to the later notion of plethories / biring–composition structures. A k-plethory is a ring with composition such that P ⊙ − is a comonad, for example k[e] and Λ. These were developed by Tall–Wraith (1970) and Borger–Wieland (2005) without reference to this 1982 composition-ring viewpoint.
missed.quote: Variante: Si A est une k-algèbre, on peut prendre ... Ω_{A/k} = End(W_k(A)) — plus généralement, si 𝒜 est un Anneau commutatif sur un topos
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: This is an early, unpublished attempt by Grothendieck to axiomatize 'function rings with composition', including in a topos. It is relevant to plethystic algebra, C^∞-rings and Fermat theories, and the history of synthetic differential geometry.

missed.claim: The question of when Ω → Ω_{Ω_0} is injective (characterizing 'functional' analyseurs) is posed but left open. The topos question (Ω_𝒜)_0 ≅ Γ𝒜 is left with a '?', although it has an easy positive answer.
missed.quote: On est content quand Ω → Ω_{Ω_0} est injectif !
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor: such representation questions are standard in composition-ring theory, but Grothendieck's framing via schemes and topoi is not on record.

deep.surprise_reason: The material is essentially the definition and basic examples of composition rings, a notion known since Menger and Adler. The novelty is only that Grothendieck independently developed it in 1982, with a scheme-theoretic and topos-theoretic twist. This is a historically interesting unpublished detail but not mathematically surprising.
transcription_corrections: 'W_k(A)' is most likely the Demazure–Gabriel functor W(A) (R ↦ A⊗_k R), not Witt vectors.
The left-margin note reads roughly 'analyseurs "ensemblistes" ou "standard" sur un pré-anneau A', naming the examples App(A,A).
The line after k[[T]]^+ reads roughly '(l'anneau des cts réduit à zéro / ou les constantes — non associatif)', i.e. the constants of k[[T]]^+ are 0, and allowing constant terms breaks composition.
